name: Māori
variant: Standard te reo Māori with macrons (Te Taura Whiri orthography); regional forms (e.g. Kāi Tahu k for ng) mentioned, not taught
script: Latin with extra letters: long vowels ā, ē, ī, ō, ū (tohutō / macrons) and the digraphs wh and ng; left to right
basis: NZ Ministry of Education Curriculum Guidelines for Teaching and Learning Te Reo Māori, levels 1–2 achievement objectives, with the grammar of the levels 1–2 Grammar Progression Table (Te Whakaipurangi Rauemi); topics in the order of Te Kākano (Te Whanake 1)

note: The curriculum guidelines give the topics (greetings, introductions, numbers and dates, personal information including iwi and pepeha, location, polite and classroom language; then relationships, possessions, likes, time and weather, descriptions and feelings) and the progression table gives the grammar, but neither puts the grammar in a teaching order; the order of lessons inside each stage is my own judgment and common course practice (verbless sentences before verbal ones, kei te before the other tense markers). Food, shopping and directions come from the Te Kākano chapter situations and common practice. The marae and pepeha lessons follow the guidelines' level 1–2 themes and text types (te marae, pepeha, whakapapa); they touch personal identity (iwi, hapū, whakapapa, marae protocol) and must be reviewed and approved by Māori reviewers before any lesson is written; a learner who is not Māori should not be taught to claim a maunga, awa or iwi. Every Māori word in the titles was spelled by me, not copied from a source, and should be checked by a speaker.
hardest: Long vowels change meaning (keke 'cake', kēkē 'armpit'), so macrons must be heard and written
Particles before the verb carry the tense: kei te, i, ka, kua, e … ana
Two kinds of possession: tāku / tōku (a- and o-class), with neutral taku
Four words for 'we': tāua, māua, tātou, mātou (two or more, with or without the listener)

items: Sounds and spelling: five vowels, long vowels with macrons (ā), wh and ng
Greetings and farewells: Kia ora, Tēnā koe / kōrua / koutou, Mōrena, Haere rā, E noho rā
Introducing yourself: Ko wai tō ingoa? Ko … tōku ingoa
Where you are from: Nō hea koe? Nō Porirua au
Polite and classroom language: Aroha mai, Ka pai, He aha te kupu Māori mō…?
Pronouns: au, koe, ia; tāua, māua, tātou, mātou
Identifying with ko: Ko Manu ia, Ko wai ia?
Classifying with he: He kaiako ia, He aha tēnei?
tēnei, tēnā, tērā: this, that (by you), that (over there)
te and ngā: one and many (te whare, ngā whare; tamaiti, tamariki)
Saying 'not' without a verb: Ehara ia i a Manu
Numbers, days and dates: tahi, rua, toru … tekau, kotahi rau; Rāhina … Rātapu
Location and directions: Kei hea a Manu? Kei te kāinga au; ki matau, ki mauī
Now: Kei te + verb (Kei te haere au), Kei te pēhea koe?
Other tense markers: i (past), ka (will), kua (has), e … ana (is …ing)
Questions: aha, wai, pēhea, hea, hia; Kei te aha a Manu?
Saying 'not' with verbs: Kāore a Manu i te kai
Objects with i and ki: Kei te kai a Manu i te āporo
Commands: E kai!, Kōrero!, Pānuitia te pukapuka!
Time and weather: He aha te wā? Kei te ua
Possessives and ownership: taku / aku, tō / ō, tana / ana; nā and nō
Likes and dislikes, with reasons: pai, nā te mea
Describing people and feelings: te whare whero, Kei te hiakai au, Kei te pōuri ia
Food and shopping: parāoa, tī, kawhe; E hia te utu?
Visiting a marae: pōwhiri, karanga, whaikōrero, hongi
Pepeha: maunga, awa, waka, iwi, and how a learner who is not Māori introduces themselves
